# Ordering

The answer a three-way comparison gives: which side is smaller, or that neither is.

```rux
pub enum Ordering: int8 {
    Less = -1,
    Equal = 0,
    Greater = 1
}
```

The discriminants are `-1`, `0` and `1` stored in an [`int8`](/docs/api/core/integers#int8), so an ordering costs one byte and its sign is the
comparison's sign. A comparison that cannot decide has no representation here: every pair a comparison is asked
about must land on exactly one of these three.
`Ordering` is a `Copy` value, so reading one never consumes it.

## Cases

| Name      | Value | Description                                  |
| --------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `Less`    | `-1`  | The left value comes before the right one.   |
| `Equal`   | `0`   | Neither comes first; the two order the same. |
| `Greater` | `1`   | The left value comes after the right one.    |

## Methods

<h3 id="is-less"><code>IsLess</code></h3>

```rux
pub func IsLess(self: &Ordering) -> bool
```

Reports whether the left side of the comparison was the smaller one.
Borrows the ordering through `self` and leaves it untouched.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: whether this ordering is `Less`

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Core/Src/Ordering.rux#L26)

<h3 id="is-equal"><code>IsEqual</code></h3>

```rux
pub func IsEqual(self: &Ordering) -> bool
```

Reports whether the two sides compared equal.
Borrows the ordering through `self` and leaves it untouched.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: whether this ordering is `Equal`

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Core/Src/Ordering.rux#L38)

<h3 id="is-greater"><code>IsGreater</code></h3>

```rux
pub func IsGreater(self: &Ordering) -> bool
```

Reports whether the left side of the comparison was the larger one.
Borrows the ordering through `self` and leaves it untouched.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: whether this ordering is `Greater`

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Core/Src/Ordering.rux#L50)

<h3 id="is-less-or-equal"><code>IsLessOrEqual</code></h3>

```rux
pub func IsLessOrEqual(self: &Ordering) -> bool
```

Reports whether the left side was smaller than or equal to the right.
Borrows the ordering through `self` and leaves it untouched. This is the negation of [`IsGreater`](/docs/api/core/ordering#is-greater), spelled out
so a caller testing a bound does not have to negate one.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: whether this ordering is `Less` or `Equal`

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Core/Src/Ordering.rux#L63)

<h3 id="is-greater-or-equal"><code>IsGreaterOrEqual</code></h3>

```rux
pub func IsGreaterOrEqual(self: &Ordering) -> bool
```

Reports whether the left side was larger than or equal to the right.
Borrows the ordering through `self` and leaves it untouched. This is the negation of [`IsLess`](/docs/api/core/ordering#is-less).
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: whether this ordering is `Greater` or `Equal`

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Core/Src/Ordering.rux#L75)

<h3 id="reverse"><code>Reverse</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Reverse(self: Ordering) -> Ordering
```

The ordering the same comparison would have given with its two sides swapped.
Consumes the ordering by value and returns a new one; `Less` and `Greater` trade places while `Equal` is its
own reverse. A `Copy` value, so the caller's own ordering is unaffected.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the opposite ordering, with `Equal` unchanged

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Core/Src/Ordering.rux#L88)
